title: Real-Time Imaging of Li-Ion Diffusion and Phase Boundary Movement in Solid-State Batteries Using Operando STEM-EELS
content: Lithium titanate (Li4+xTi5O12: LTO) is widely recognized as a promising anode material for solid-state Li-ion batteries, primarily due to its high redox potential (∼1.55 V vs. Li) and excellent structural stability during cycling [1,2]. Although LTO undergoes a two-phase transition between Li4Ti5O12 and Li7Ti5O12, it still exhibits favorable high-rate performance. This apparent contradiction—low Li-ion diffusivity in the end-member phases (Li4Ti5O12 and Li7Ti5O12) versus rapid charge/discharge capability—suggests that important kinetic processes take place at the phase boundary or within localized regions, such as surfaces, grain boundaries, or defects [3–5]. Elucidating these mechanisms is essential for improving LTO and similar materials that rely on two-phase reactions. In this study, we employed operando scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) coupled with electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) to directly visualize the phase boundary kinetics in LTO [6]. By preparing thin lamellae of the LTO particle in a solid-state cell configuration, we captured real-time and real-space images of Li distribution changes during both Li insertion (charging) and Li extraction (discharging). The STEM-EELS approach provides simultaneous structural and chemical information: atomic number contrast via annular dark-field (ADF) imaging, and element-specific spectra (including the Li K, Ti L, and O K edges) to detect changes in oxidation state and Li concentration [7].
